overview: Federal agents recently observed a mysterious flying triangle near a secure U.S. facility. Wall Street and major banks are preparing for artificial intelligence worst-case scenarios and its aftermath. Meanwhile, soaring prices have not broken America's entrenched diesel habit. In San Francisco, local elections feature discussions on props aimed at cleaning up City Hall and early state senate bids. In Hawaii, news covers a new plan for the Honolulu rail line, a massive Kalihi redevelopment project, and a false claims law.

items.title: Mysterious "flying triangle" sighting leads new government release of UFO documents
items.summary: Federal agents near a secure facility sighted an unidentified matte black triangle that moved quickly and made no sound.

items.title: Wall Street prepares for AI's "day after"
items.summary: Major banks and financial institutions are collaborating with AI companies to prepare for potential catastrophe scenarios.

items.title: Why soaring prices aren't breaking America's diesel habit
items.summary: Despite historically high prices, diesel remains deeply entrenched in farming, trucking, and other industries.

items.title: Election ad fact-check: Will Props. D, E, and F really ‘Clean up City Hall’?
items.summary: Mission Local investigates the dire warnings and big promises made in advertisements for Props D, E, and F.

items.title: Election Extra! Matt Haney gets started early for state senate bid
items.summary: Matt Haney announced endorsements from 52 fellow California Assembly members for his bid for a state senate seat.

items.title: New Plan Aims To Extend Honolulu Rail Line For An Extra $4 Billion
items.summary: A subcommittee tentatively endorsed extending the Honolulu rail line system to Ala Moana Center and Kapolei for $4 billion.

items.title: 10-tower redevelopment project takes shape in Kalihi
items.summary: A new 10-tower redevelopment project is taking shape in Kalihi, offering a chance for residents to move back.

items.title: Hawaiʻi Citizens Have A Powerful Law On The Books To Combat Fraud
items.summary: Hawaiʻi citizens have the State False Claims Act available to prosecute companies and individuals profiting from lax oversight.
